score_rationale_2026_06_13: Re-scored 6.5 -> 7.5 after verifying that ec7fe2f6 genuinely closed all seven P1 go-live blockers (each with a passing acceptance test; B-01 read down to its recovery-marker test). Held below 8 by 22 OPEN + 6 PARTIAL P2/P3 items (no stream idle watchdog, per-turn breaker, microcompact ask_user answer-loss, no /readyz, no Windows CI, no agent-core fuzz/bench/mutation). score_rationale: The agent CORE LOOP is genuinely production-grade (8.5/10 in isolation): TOCTOU-safe shared-atomic budget, race-clean iter.Seq2 with airtight yield-after-false discipline, two-tier dedup with progress veto, real circuit breaker checked before each call, bounded per-call/per-tool timeouts, untrusted-output provenance envelope (NFKC + HTML-escape + crypto/rand nonce), capped subprocess buffers, symlink-resistant workspace fences. The 2026-06-10/11 P0/P1 remediation is REAL work, not paperwork — most prior closures verify. The score is held down by the PRODUCTION PERIMETER, which this re-audit finds materially weaker than the prior cycle credited: (a) crash-durability gap — mutating tool side effects re-execute after an intra-turn crash (R-05 only half-closed); (b) the serve daemon never boots the tracer and the agent core has no structured logging and no latency/error/cost metrics, so production runs operationally BLIND; (c) no per-thread in-flight guard — concurrent runs on one thread corrupt conversation history; (d) a new trust-boundary hole — swarm child reports re-enter the parent prompt unwrapped; (e) no production container (non-root, resource-bounded) for a runtime that executes arbitrary shell. Core 8.5, perimeter ~4.5 → blended 6.5. Closing the P1 set lands 7.5-8.

findings_by_status_2026_06_13.note: 2026-06-13 PM: the 6 PARTIAL findings were worked TDD-first — 5 CLOSED (B-07,B-13,O-04,B-15,T-03), M-06 advanced to rotation-done (periodic sidecar sweep pending). B-11 is CLOSED only nominally (shell_exec.go at 599/600 LOC). Reliability cluster CLOSED: B-05 (breaker hoisted to a Runner process-lifetime singleton), B-06 (breaker-open routes to finalize, not the iter.Seq2 error slot), B-08 (stream idle watchdog AURA_LLM_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC, keep-alive-resilient, emits retryable ErrStreamIdleTimeout). Memory cluster: M-01 CLOSED (L1 microcompact only evicts sidecar-backed tool turns), M-02 CLOSED via gate-first reorder (MarkResumed before inject — a duplicate resume returns ErrPauseNotFound before any second answer turn; meets AP-9 acceptance, full single-tx deferred by user decision, residual mark-then-inject-fail window documented). M-03 CLOSED via a nanobot-style hardCap floor for small windows: when the SPEC Req#10 formula is non-positive (window below the ~33k fixed reservation, e.g. Slice-13 vLLM) hardCap() clamps to a positive ContextWindow/2 instead of 0, so L2.5 truncation stays active rather than silently returning raw history; only a ContextWindow<=0 misconfig still yields 0 (boot fail-fast is the seam to reject it). M-07 CLOSED: both anyInt copies (runner_persist.go + cmd/aura/chat_render.go) now carry a json.Number case parsing via .Int64() (fall through to 0 on parse error), so a UseNumber-decoded StateDelta or a jsonb round-trip no longer silently zeroes token-count usage rows. R-41 CLOSED: a tools.SessionEvictor interface (Evict(sessionID), idempotent + self-locked) is implemented by the three genuinely session-keyed holders — TodoTool.byID, ShellExec.cwd, ShellApprovals.{approved,pending} — and Runner.Stop now ranges the tool registry (All()) calling Evict(convID) (sessionID==conversationID per D-26), so a long-running serve daemon reclaims a finished conversation's tool state instead of leaking it (shell_bg's BackgroundShells is keyed by sh_N not sessionID and already self-prunes, so it is intentionally untouched). M-04 CLOSED: AppendTurn + AppendAssistantTurnWithCacheMetric now wrap their db.WithTx in cleanupSidecarOnTxError(run, spilledPath) — when the turn-append tx errors (rollback) the just-spilled sidecar file is best-effort os.Remove'd (path captured via a closure so the seq-allocated-inside-tx branch is covered too), so a rolled-back oversized turn no longer leaves an orphan file alive for the rest of a long-running daemon; the boot orphan scan (orphan_scan.go) remains the backstop and the success path is untouched (the file is the committed turn's durable content). Proven RED->GREEN by a unit-seam test (no live DB): appendTurnWrites does the real spill, the injectable tx step forces a post-spill rollback, os.Stat asserts removal-on-error and keep-on-success. O-03 CLOSED: the process-global otel.SetErrorHandler no-op (tracing.go otlp branch) that silently swallowed every OTel SDK error (export failures, queue-full drops) was replaced by a rate-limited slog handler installed in obs.Init's shared boot path (internal/obs/otel_error_handler.go) — so it covers every exporter mode (otlp/stdout/none), not just otlp. It logs each error WARN at most once per window (60s default), folding the rest into a suppressed counter surfaced on the next emission, so a broken exporter cannot flood the logs while real trace loss is no longer invisible. Clock is injectable for deterministic tests; nil logger falls back to slog.Default(). TDD-first: TestRateLimitedOTelHandler_{FirstErrorLogged,BurstWithinWindowSuppressed,NextWindowReportsSuppressedCount,FirstLogOmitsSuppressedWhenZero,NilLoggerDefaultsToSlogDefault} went RED (undefined handler) before, GREEN after. O-05 CLOSED: the serve daemon's health endpoint was Postgres-only liveness with no graph/provider readiness and no /readyz, so a load balancer could route to an instance whose required Neo4j backend was down. Added a GET /readyz readiness endpoint in internal/agui over an injectable ReadinessProbe seam ({Name, Check func(ctx) error} list on ServerConfig): each probe runs under a bounded 3s ctx, /readyz answers 200 only when ALL required deps pass, else 503 with a terse JSON body naming each failed dep (error string sanitized through SanitizeString so a bolt DSN never leaks). serve.go wires two real probes — postgres (the open pgx pool's Ping) and neo4j (knowledge.VerifyConnectivity, a native-driver dial+VerifyConnectivity+Close, no long-lived handle since the daemon holds no persistent graph client). /healthz stays the cheap PG-only liveness check, deliberately NOT flipped by a down readiness dep (Open-Q #2: an MCP-free `aura chat` is not hard-coupled to graph availability; only the SERVE daemon's readiness reflects required backends). TDD-first: TestServerReadyz/{all probes healthy->200,a failing probe->503 naming the dep,no probes configured->200,healthz stays 200 when a readiness dep is down} went RED (undefined ReadinessProbe field) before, GREEN after. O-08 CLOSED: OTel span coverage was llm.request-only (one span per LLM call, no per-turn or per-tool span), so a trace could not show per-turn or per-tool latency (AP-20). Added an agent.turn span wrapping the whole Run loop (started before the iter.Seq2 closure, ended on EVERY return path via a deferred endTurnSpan over the closure with a turnReason terminal-outcome attribute) plus a tool.execute span per dispatch in runTool (attrs tool.name/tool.mutating/tool.success/tool.error). Both the existing llm.request span and the new tool.execute span now nest under agent.turn — the turn ctx is threaded through ic.WithContext(turnCtx) so callCtx (llm.request) and the tool dispatch ctx (tool.execute) parent off it. Span helpers live in tracing.go (startTurnSpan/endTurnSpan/startToolSpan/endToolSpan); creation stays cheap + non-fatal (a no-op tracer mints a dropped span). TDD-first: TestSpan_TurnTreeParenting (asserts agent.turn + tool.execute[tool.name=echo] + llm.request recorded, with tool.execute/llm.request parent SpanID == agent.turn SpanID) and TestSpan_TurnEndsOnEveryPath (exactly one ended agent.turn span on the content-stop path) went RED before, GREEN after; the stale TestSpan_PerCall total-span==1 assertion was narrowed to count llm.request spans specifically (per-call contract preserved). O-06 CLOSED: a SIGTERM hard-cancelled in-flight turns (asymmetric drain) — the channel (Telegram) per-turn ctx derived from the daemon's signal NotifyContext, so a SIGTERM cancelled the turn ctx the instant the signal fired, killing a turn mid-stream instead of letting it reach a terminal frame (the HTTP/SSE path was already drained by http.Server.Shutdown, hence the asymmetry). Fix (AP-17): runServe now keeps the signal ctx as the stop-TRIGGER only (it returns scheduler.Start) and parents the actual per-turn work on a SEPARATE background-derived workCtx that the signal does NOT cancel. On the signal the daemon stops accepting NEW work (stopChannelSubsystems stops the poller + StopAll joins in-flight turn WaitGroups, httpSrv.Shutdown stops the listener) and JOINS the in-flight turns under a bounded grace window (AURA_SERVE_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SEC, default 25s) via a small testable drainWithGrace helper (cmd/aura/serve_drain.go); only AFTER the grace elapses does workCancel fire as the final hard-cancel backstop, and drainWithGrace never blocks past the grace on an overrunning turn (no wedge; a non-positive knob degrades to immediate backstop). No change to internal/runner or internal/agui — the seam is entirely at the cmd/aura composition root. TDD-first: TestDrainWithGrace_{FinishesBeforeGrace->drained+turn ran to completion,ExceedsGrace->timed-out+returns within ~grace not blocked on the straggler} went RED (undefined drainWithGrace/drainResult*) before, GREEN after. B-09 CLOSED: the secret-env-key denylist had THREE divergent local copies — shell child-env (shell_exec_env.go, markers token/secret/password/passwd/api_key/apikey/auth/bearer/credential, MISSING bare 'key'), MCP child-env (mcp/client.go, same + 'key'), MCP managed-config export (mcp/manager/config.go, token/secret/pass/key/auth/bearer/credential) — so a bare *_KEY (e.g. PRIVATE_KEY) was redacted on the MCP path but LEAKED into the shell child (AP-13). Unified onto one canonical predicate secret.IsSecretEnvKey in a new internal/secret/envkey.go, the safer SUPERSET of all three (markers key/token/secret/pass/auth/bearer/credential + audit-mandated private/cert; 'key' subsumes api_key/apikey/private_key/ssh_key, 'pass' subsumes password/passwd/passphrase); all three call sites now call it and the three local copies are deleted. TDD-first: a table test for IsSecretEnvKey (asserts the canonical secret set matches AND PATH/HOME/LANG/AURA_LOOP_MAX_STEPS do NOT over-redact) plus a shell-path acceptance test went RED (PRIVATE_KEY observed in the shell child env) before, GREEN after; a matching MCP-path test locks the cross-site equivalence. B-10 CLOSED: the destructive-shell approval gate was OFF by default (unset AURA_SHELL_DESTRUCTIVE_PATTERNS -> NO patterns, so rm -rf / ran unattended). Now ON BY DEFAULT as an ADVISORY guardrail (AP-15): an unset env var falls back to a conservative built-in set (defaultDestructivePatterns in shell_exec_env.go — rm -rf on a root/top-level path, mkfs.*, dd of=/dev/*, the classic fork bomb, redirect-truncate into a raw block device), narrow on purpose so an ordinary rm file.txt / go test / git status is never gated. Documented as advisory NOT a security boundary (regex over the raw command line is phrase-around-able; the real boundary is host/sandbox policy + the operator's own privileges) in a doc comment on the env const and defaultDestructivePatterns. Stays overridable: an explicit value REPLACES the default (no merge), the empty string or 'off' is the explicit opt-out. TDD-first: TestDestructiveShellDefaultOnFlagsRmRf went RED (unset env -> rm -rf / actually EXECUTED, 10.6s) then GREEN (gated in 0.16s, never runs); TestDestructiveShellDefaultPatternsCoverConservativeSet (destructive set matches, benign does not) + TestDestructiveShellDefaultIsOverridable ('off' disables, custom replaces-not-merges). B-14 CLOSED: Registry.Register silently OVERWROTE a previously-registered tool with the same name (a programming error swallowed, a name collision shadowing a tool). Now FAILS LOUD with a panic at registration time (the net/http duplicate-route idiom; no error return because no caller can recover from a static wiring collision). Surfaced a REAL latent double-registration the silent overwrite had been masking: cmd/aura replayAudit (cache_audit.go) called buildRegistry() — which already wires a default `skill` tool — then registered its own deterministic `skill`, so the audit's was silently replacing the default; fixed minimally with the existing tools.Without(buildRegistry(), skillManifestName) to drop the default before registering the deterministic one (preserves the audit's intent). All other call sites use distinct names; runtime never re-registers (registration is boot-time only; ToolSearch reads the registry, never mounts). TDD-first: TestRegisterDuplicateNamePanics went RED (silent overwrite, no panic) then GREEN (panics naming the colliding tool); TestRegisterDistinctNamesSucceeds locks the normal path. Commits in reconciliation-2026-06-13.md.
